item.title: Nissan Silvia (1965)
item.description:
Publication: Car Graphic
Format: Road Impression
Date: May 1965
Author: Keiichiro Ichikawa

Conclusions from a 1,000km Road Test

Now, as I sit down to put together this test report on the Silvia, I feel that I have come to understand its “character” completely. That is because I have driven it to my heart’s content through crowded city streets, over the rough and uneven roads of Chiba and Ibaraki Prefectures, and along the winding roads that follow the ridges of Hakone and Izu.

item.title: Nissan Silvia (1965)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Magazine
Format: Road Impression
Date: May 1965
Author: Hideo Aoki

“Silvia”—a name belonging to a beautiful woman in Greek mythology, and said to have inspired numerous artistic works, including Schubert’s song “To Sylvia” and Delibes’ “Sylvia” ballet suite. I must admit that it was a name I had never heard before, although its pleasing sound led me to imagine that it must have something to do with beauty.

We tested the Silvia on March 20 at the Yatabe High-Speed Test Course. I should make it clear, however, that this was not a road test in the usual sense. Given the location, it was necessarily more of a high-speed test. I hope to carry out a more detailed road test at a later date.

item.title: Nissan Silvia (1965)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Magazine
Format: Engineering Interview
Date: May 1965
Authors (roundtable): Kazumi Yotsumoto, Hideo Aoki, Hiromichi Nakamura, Tomoharu Izumi, Seijiro Matsumoto, Kenichi Sasaki, Osamu Machida, Motor Magazine editorial staff (uncredited)

Roundtable Discussion: Talking with Nissan About the Silvia

Magazine: When the Silvia prototype was exhibited at last year’s Motor Show, its bold styling and the specifications that were partially disclosed gave us the impression that this would be a sports car with considerably higher performance than we had imagined.

item.title: Nissan Silvia (1965)
item.description:
Publication: Auto Sport
Format: Road Test Report
Date: Summer 1965
Author: Hiroshi Hoshijima

The Silvia Aims to Be “A Beautiful Car”

I had the opportunity to drive the Silvia for five laps of the Yatabe high-speed test course, as well as on a round trip from Tokyo to Kyoto, and would like to report my impressions. This was the first time that a fully registered Silvia had been driven over such a long distance.

item.title: Nissan Silvia (1965)
item.description:
Publication: Motor Fan
Format: Road Test
Date: July 1965
Authors (Roundtable): Teiichi Hara, Motoo Harada, Osamu Hirao, Hiromichi Nakamura, Kenzaburo Ishikawa, Kazuo Kumabe, Masaichi Kondo, Kazumi Yotsumoto, Mineo Yamamoto, Yasuhei Oguchi, Atsushi Watari, Naoyuki Yamada, Taizo Tateishi, Akio Miyamoto, Kenji Higuchi

A High-Performance Car to Match the Styling

Magazine: Since last year’s Tokyo Motor Show, the Silvia has generated quite a bit of attention, and now it has finally gone on sale. It seems to differ considerably from the prototype that was exhibited at the show, so let’s begin with an explanation of the development aims from Nissan.
